name: Jordanian Arabic (Ammani)
notes: Jordanian Arabic — Ammani koine, a new dialect formed from Jordanian + urban Palestinian contact (Al-Wer 2020). INPUT CONTRACT: fully-diacritized Arabic. ق qaf is a socially reallocated variable: [ɡ] (traditional Jordanian, much male speech) alongside [ʔ] (urban Palestinian / the emerging Ammani prestige — third-generation women use [ʔ] consistently, men use both: Al-Wer 2020:560). Both are listed, ɡ first as the distinctively Jordanian value. ج jim → [dʒ]~[ʒ] (men vary, women [ʒ]: Al-Wer 2020:560). Interdentals: the Ammani koine favours the merged stops [t d dˤ] (Al-Wer 2020:560; Fadda 2016:27-28 — the koine consonant system is 'identical to other Levantine cities'); the interdental variants persist in traditional Jordanian/Bedouin speech and remain in the inventory via the parent. Vowels /i u a/ + /iː uː eː oː aː/ and /aj aw/→[eː oː] (bajt→beːt, sˤawt→sˤoːtˤ: Fadda 2016:30) are inherited from the Levantine parent. MEASURED UNDECIDABLE-INPUT CEILING. Exactly one of the 3182 WikiPron ajp_arab_broad input words carries any ḥaraka at all (حمّيضة, and the mark is a shadda); not a single word in the file carries a short-vowel mark — while the gold transcriptions are fully vocalised: 30.6% of their phoneme segments are short vowels. Deleting every short vowel from the gold and rescoring with the harness's own scorer gives PER 0.2648 over 2513 scored words (scripts/omission_score.py, which computes it through the scorer's own normalisation and edit distance), which is what a spec that emitted perfect consonants and long vowels and simply omitted the short vowels would score, and is therefore the omission score for this row. An omission score is not a lower bound. Deleting a segment and guessing it wrong cost the same single edit, so a spec that guesses the likeliest value beats omission whenever the guess lands, and rows do come in below it. The board row stands at 0.3451, so about 8.0 PER points separate the score from the omission score. That gap is rule error and is tractable; the omission score covers undecidable input that no grapheme table can recover. A gap above the omission score is a defect hypothesis, not an excuse: Hebrew sat above its own omission score for what looked like the same structural reason and the excess turned out to be a real defect, an unmapped geresh. That vocalisation and not the grapheme tables dominates the Arabic error is measured on the MSA row rather than inferred: ar scores PER 0.3139 on raw WikiPron and 0.1721 on the SAME gold with the input auto-diacritized (the wikipron_ar_diacritized row, wired in scripts/benchmark.py) — within a hundredth of the 0.1656 the spec scores on the material the orthography does supply, its folded PER, which scripts/folded_per.py computes and its valid_ceiling records. Vocalisation is worth about 14 PER points there, more than any grapheme-table change could be worth. No dialect row has such a companion: the diacritized loader is registered for ar alone, and wiring one for this row is the single highest-value follow-up available to it. It has to be labelled restored-MSA input rather than native vocalisation — the restorer targets MSA and Classical Arabic, so what it writes onto dialect orthography is an MSA reading, and a row scored against it measures the spec plus that assumption. MATRES LECTIONIS AFTER A CONSONANT. ⟨و⟩ and ⟨ي⟩ after a consonant letter are read first as the long vowels [uː] and [iː], then [oː] and [eː], then the glides [w] and [j]; word-initially and after a vowel they stay glides. Exception: the inherited keys َوِ and َيِ take the kasra, so a word-final ⟨ي⟩ after them would look like it follows a vowel; the positional keys َوِي and َيِي read it as the long vowel [iː] at word end (قَوِي [awiː]) and keep the glide elsewhere (قَوِيَّة [awijja]). Wikipedia 'Levantine Arabic', Orthography and writing systems, table Vowels (source levantine_arabic_wiki): ـُو ū [uː] 'as in food'; ـِي ī [iː] 'as in see'; ـَو ō [oː]; ـَي ē [eː]. The same table gives short [u] and [i] for ـُو and ـِي in rows the table marks as respelled or shorter, so the glide and short readings stay as later candidates. Gold count (WikiPron ar-JO, 3182 lines; rows with the letter after a consonant): ⟨و⟩ 348 rows, which hold uː 107, oː 83, w 202 segments; ⟨ي⟩ 549 rows, which hold iː 203, eː 67, j 270 segments. These are segments inside those rows, not a per-letter alignment, and the glide counts include diphthongs and glides elsewhere in the same rows. ADJACENT LETTERS AND THE FINAL TA MARBUTA. Read one letter at a time, the after_consonant rule made both letters of يو and وي long vowels (بيوت biːuːt), and it made ⟨و⟩ and ⟨ي⟩ before a final ة long vowels (قهوة with uː). The grapheme keys يو [juː, joː, iːw], وي [wiː, weː, uːj], ية [ja, jat], وة [wa, wat], وية [uːja, wja] and يوة [iːwa, eːwa, jwa] read the first of two adjacent letters as the glide, and a letter before a final ة as the glide. Gold count (WikiPron ar-JO): 3182 lines. After a consonant letter, the pair (row counts by the reading in the transcription): وي glide+long 7; وي other 14; يو glide+long 3; يو long+glide 1; يو other 4. Word-final after a consonant letter: وة glide 4; ية glide 67. Wikipedia 'Levantine Arabic' (source levantine_arabic_wiki), read 2026-09-13 in the raw wikitext: under nouns and adjectives, nisba adjectives "Their feminine form ends in ـية -iyye", so ⟨ي⟩ before the final ة is the glide; under pronouns, "جاب الجريدة لأبوي jāb il-jarīde la-ʔabūy", where ⟨و⟩ after a consonant letter is the long vowel and the ⟨ي⟩ after it is the glide. That is the وي candidate uːj, which this spec ranks third: لأبوي gives ˈlʔabwiː, so this line does not support the ranking of the وي key.

sources.notes: READ in full. Amman koine: (q) is a socially reallocated variable, [ɡ] (Jordanian) ~ [ʔ] (urban Palestinian); gen-III women use [ʔ] consistently, men both (p.560). (ǧ) jim: [dʒ]~[ʒ], women [ʒ] (p.560). Interdentals: both genders favour stop variants (p.560).

sources.author: Fadda, H.
sources.title: Language Variation in Western Amman
sources.publisher: MA thesis, Canada Institute of Linguistics (CanIL)
sources.notes: READ (phonology chapter). Ammani koine consonants = urban Palestinian [ʔ t d dˤ ʒ], 'identical to other Levantine cities' (pp.27-28). Qaf labels (Al-Wer & Herin 2011:60): [g] gilit, [q] qeltu, [ʔ] Jerusalem, [k] rural West Bank. Vowels: short /i u a/, long /iː uː eː oː aː/ (Al-Wer 2011:4). Diphthongs /aj aw/→[eː oː] except before glide: bajt→beːt, sˤawt→sˤoːtˤ (p.30).

sources.author: Almbark, R. & Hellmuth, S.
sources.title: Acoustic analysis of the Syrian Arabic vowel system
sources.notes: READ in full. Damascus/Syrian vowel system: five long /iː eː aː oː uː/, three short contrastive /i a u/; mid short [e o] and schwa are allophones of /i u/ (§3-4). Mid-long /eː oː/ from /aj aw/ coalescence (§1.1). /aː/ higher/fronter in Coastal Syria than Damascus (p.2).

stress.notes: Arabic stress is QUANTITY-SENSITIVE: it falls on a syllable because that syllable is heavy, not because of any orthographic ending, so no ending table can express it. The cascade (Ryding, A Reference Grammar of MSA, CUP 2005, §2.3; Watson, The Phonology and Morphology of Arabic, OUP 2002, ch.3): a superheavy final syllable (CVːC/CVCC) takes the stress (kiˈtaːb); otherwise a heavy penult (CVː/CVC) does (muˈdarris); otherwise the antepenult (ˈmadrasa). max_onset=1 because Arabic onsets are obligatory and hold exactly one consonant — a medial cluster splits, closing the preceding syllable, and that boundary is what makes the penult of mudarris heavy. INPUT CONTRACT: weight is only recoverable from a complete transcription, so this requires diacritized input; an undiacritized skeleton has no vowels to weigh. The registered wikipron gold carries no stress marks, but the benchmark strips stress from both sides by default, so this costs no PER. Prosodic clitics: monosyllabic function words (negator maː, prepositions fiː/min/ʕan/ʕa/li/bi, vocative jaː, copula-negator muː/miʃ, conditional law/loː, wa-proclitic combinations) attach to a host and fall inside the host's stress domain, so they carry no word stress (Watson 2002, The Phonology and Morphology of Arabic, OUP, ch.3). Pan-Arabic class; the per-lect form list reflects the function words attested in this lect. Orthographic test — a clitic homograph (e.g. verb yā 'came') is destressed in every occurrence.

wikipron.measured: 1 of 3182 wikipron input words (ajp_arab_broad.tsv) carries any harakat mark at all, and that one is a shadda gemination mark, not a short vowel (حمّيضة); 0 carry a short-vowel diacritic. Wiktionary files Arabic entries at the unvocalized page title (Wiktionary:About_Arabic / Wiktionary:Arabic_entry_guidelines, 'Entry name'), so the scraped input is a consonant-plus-long-vowel skeleton, exactly the pattern independently measured on the bare 'ar' wikipron row (0/17,563 words carry a haraka there; see ar.json audit.wikipron). No fold was run for this dialect row -- doing so needs the dialect's own vowel inventory, not MSA's -- so no valid_ceiling is recorded here; the wikipron_ar_diacritized loader (scripts/benchmark.py) that would supply it is wired for the 'ar' row only.
